description:
pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs:118, 158, 194

Each call to `web_pki_policy()`, `smime_policy()`, and `code_signing_policy()` calls `CABF_ALLOWED_ALGS.to_vec()` which allocates a fresh `Vec<ObjectIdentifier>` on the heap from a `&'static [ObjectIdentifier]` slice.

This is called every time a policy object is constructed — potentially on every connection in a TLS server. Since the list is always the same static content, there are two cleaner alternatives:

1. Change `ValidationPolicy::allowed_signature_algs` from `Option<Vec<OID>>` to `Option<Arc<[OID]>>` or `Option<Cow<'static, [OID]>>`. The `Cow` approach would allow profiles to hold a `Borrowed` reference to the static slice at zero allocation cost.

2. Accept the current design as-is with a comment explaining that policy objects are intended to be constructed once (e.g., at server startup) and shared via `Arc<ValidationPolicy>`. Add that note to the `ValidationPolicy` doc.

The current behavior is not incorrect but contradicts the general Rust principle of avoiding gratuitous allocations on frequently-called paths.

Note: This also affects `required_leaf_eku` fields: `Some(vec![ID_KP_SERVER_AUTH])` allocates a single-element Vec on each call.
notes: ValidationPolicy is intended to be constructed once at startup. Deferred; doc note added to ValidationPolicy.
title: pkix-profiles: CABF_ALLOWED_ALGS.to_vec() allocates on every policy construction — consider Cow or Arc
